claim.summary: Under certificate-cube-erasure hypotheses, for every integer t>=1 put P=ordered product(1-F_i), H=sum_i prefix(1-F_j)Y_i and G_t=sum_(j<t)P^j. The supplied certificate C transforms to D_t=G_t H+P^t C, a certificate preserving placeholder-linearity, of size O(S+(m+t^2+1)(s+m+1)) and ordered unbounded-fan-in depth <=max(d,delta+4)+2. At every Boolean old point a, D_t-G_t H lies in the t-th power of the two-sided old-point ideal, so old-variable jets of order<t have the common small implicit representative G_t H. This is iterated cube normalization; it does not construct a certificate from nothing, enumerate all jets, preserve original degree/exact depth, or prove exact simulation-image preservation.
claim.assessment: Working costed iteration of the existing normalization, passed by the same fresh GPT-6.1-Sol medium reviewer after staged architecture comparison. No explicit jet-list or exact simulation-image complexity claim.

claim.summary: For any IPS certificate C and chosen input generator F0, D=(1-F0)C+Y0 is a certificate with D=Y0 modulo (1-F0), size O(S+sizeF0+1) and constant added depth. It preserves Hilbert-likeness and applies to any substitution sending F0 to one. In the specified binary sequent simulation, left weakening the final contradiction by input A0, moving it right by negation and cutting with a fresh input leaf compiles exactly to D. Three inference steps and one leaf suffice. Thus the unit-slice erasure is available inside this simulation image, including bounded-depth rank input formulas; no shallow refutation is constructed from nothing.
